subject: Post-demo: unit-cost breakdown & proposed benchmarking (batching + cache)
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya@nimblecart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Post-demo: unit-cost breakdown & proposed benchmarking (batching + cache)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so your team can evaluate the unit economics cleanly: 

Summary of what we covered
- Redwood strengths: predictable per-token economics with dynamic batching, prefix/KV cache to reduce repeat token costs, and automated routing to lower-cost model variants under load.
- Hyperscaler tradeoffs we discussed: managed endpoints have simple pricing but less control over batching/cache knobs; some models have lower raw latency but higher per-token cost at scale due to throttled batching.

Requested deliverables (my action items)
1) Share a compact unit-econ workbook that lets you model: per-1M tokens, effective tokens after cache hits, and cost sensitivity to batch size. (attached)
2) Proposed side-by-side benchmark tests we can run against your sample traffic: three experiments (details below).
3) Provide a temporary test account and a short script to replay nimble-sample-traffic.csv to compare Redwood hosted + Dedicated vs your current hyperscaler baseline.

Proposed experiments (we recommend running these in parallel to reduce noise)
A) Sequence-length sensitivity: run identical prompts at 64/256/1024 token cutoffs and capture per-token latency and cost.
B) Batching curve: sweep batch sizes [1, 4, 8, 16, 32] with typical concurrency to surface throughput vs tail-latency and unit-cost.
C) Cache hit modeling: run with an initial cold-cache pass then a warm run (simulate 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% cache hit rates) to show marginal token savings and cost impact.

What we need from you
- A sample traffic file (we used the anonymized nimble-sample-traffic.csv you shared) and a short list of representative prompts/sequence-length buckets.
- Approval to spin a short Dedicated pool for a 48-hour window (if you want to see Dedicated economics; otherwise we can run hosted).

Next steps & timing
- I’ll load the workbook and a test harness this afternoon and post access details.
- Can we run the tests next Wed–Thu (June 23–24)? That gives your SRE time to approve test IPs.

Attachments: redwood-unit-econ-playbook.xlsx (workbook), nimble-sample-traffic.csv (anonymized sample)

Thanks — I’ll follow up with the test harness link later today.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Appreciate the recap and workbook. Quick clarifications from our side: 
- We’re particularly sensitive to cache semantics — our cart microservice generates many short repeats (order summaries). If you can show realistic savings for >50% hit rates that will move the needle.
- For Dedicated: budget team needs a clear delta vs our current Vertex setup before approving. Can you provide expected per-1M token ranges (hosted vs dedicated vs our Vertex bill) for 4 different profiles (chat short, chat long, embedding, reranking)?

We can approve the test IPs by Friday if Redwood provides the IP ranges and the test harness.

Also looping in SRE to confirm they’re comfortable with the replay.

Thanks,

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:18:00 -0000
Subject: RE: NimbleCart baseline numbers (starter)

Alex / Marissa —
Here are conservative starter estimates to put in front of Priya. These assume mixed workload (60% chat short, 20% chat long, 10% embeddings, 10% rerank) and realistic batching/cache profiles (average batch size 8, cache hit 40%).

Redwood hosted: $0.95 — $1.25 per 1M effective tokens (effective = gross tokens * (1 - cache_hit))
Redwood Dedicated (reserved infra): $0.55 — $0.80 per 1M effective tokens
Vertex-equivalent managed endpoints (baseline): $1.10 — $1.60 per 1M effective tokens (depends heavily on the model family and batching control)

Notes:
- The biggest swings are batch size and cache hit. A move from batch size 1 -> 8 can cut per-token cost by ~25–40% on our workload.
- Cache moving from 0% -> 50% reduces effective tokens and clearly improves unit economics; we'll capture this in the workbook charts.

I’ll add more granular per-profile rows tomorrow (chat short/long/embedding/rerank).

Ben
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
